solves: Gives the person a one-line field to type or edit a value, such as a name, an email or a search, and takes part in the form that contains it.
use_when: When the person needs to type or edit a one-line value.
Inside an nph-field when the field needs a label, help or an error message.
With a start or end icon turned on by the property, without creating a variant.
default in general use; large on the screen that needs the 44 px target, for every field of the form and the button next to them.
compact for the search of the compact nph-toolbar and for the compact table, with mouse and keyboard.
do_not_use_when: For multi-line text: the field holds one line.
For a password, a number or a masked value: they are out of v1 and get their own task.
To show the error message or the help: they belong to nph-field.
To name the field with the placeholder alone: it disappears when the person types.
To show a value that cannot be edited: there is no read-only state.
In compact on a touch screen: its 28 px target is for mouse and keyboard only.

type.constraint: The type of the inner native field (D1). Password, number and mask are out of v1. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

size.constraint: large changes only the height: control/height-default or control/height-large. compact changes the height, input/height-compact, and the end padding, input/clear-padding-end. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the measures by it. One size per form, the same as the button next to the field.

value.constraint: The current value. The value attribute is the initial value and the value of form.reset(), as in the native input: it applies only while the person has not edited the field and setting the property has not made it dirty. Setting it from code fires no event.

placeholder.constraint: The example before typing, already localized. It is not a name: it disappears when the person types.

name.constraint: The name of the entry in the form data. Reflects because the form reads the attribute of the host: without it, the value is left out of the submission.

autocomplete.constraint: The purpose of the value for autofill, such as email or tel, passed to the inner field (WCAG 1.3.5).

required.constraint: The native required of the inner field: announced by the screen reader and checked by the form, with the message of the browser. A form whose messages are written by nph-field uses novalidate when the browser balloon is not wanted.

disabled.constraint: The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, on color/muted, out of the Tab order and of the form data. A disabled fieldset disables it too. It wins over invalid.

invalid.constraint: The error state: the border becomes status/error and the inner field gets aria-invalid. It is not a constraint of the form. The sentence belongs to nph-field; never invalid without it.

label.constraint: The accessible name in text, never visible, for a field with no associated label, such as a search on its own; nph-field writes it. An associated label (nph-label for, or a label element) wins over it.

description.constraint: The accessible description in text, never visible: the help or the error sentence that nph-field writes. It is read when the field takes focus.

icon-start.constraint: none or a core name of nph-icon, light, at icon/size-sm, before the value. Decorative. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

icon-end.constraint: none or a core name of nph-icon: it turns on the end button, which always clears the value; the name only swaps the art, xmark in Figma. The button shows only when there is a value and the field is enabled.

clear-label.constraint: The accessible name of the clear button, already localized. Required with icon-end: without it, the field renders without the button and emits console.error in development.

input.constraint: The native input event, when the person types or clears. It bubbles and crosses the shadow root. Read the value from the host.

change.constraint: The native change event, fired again by the host when the person commits a value or clears it. It bubbles. Setting value from code fires neither event.

size.choose_when: default in general use; large on the screen that needs the 44 px target for the accessibility of its users; compact for the search of the compact nph-toolbar and for the compact table, with mouse and keyboard. One size per form, the same as the button next to the field.
do_not_combine_with: Fields of different sizes in the same form.

icons.choose_when: A start icon when it says what the field takes, such as magnifying-glass in a search. The end icon when the person will often clear the value.

hover.changes_for_user: The border goes one step darker under the pointer.

focus.changes_for_user: The border takes focus/border with the focus/halo attached outside, at focus/radius-control and focus/ring-width.

focus-clear.changes_for_user: Keyboard focus on the clear button: the container keeps color/input, and the border and the halo sit around the 24 by 24 target. In compact the ring goes past the field while the button has focus.

error.changes_for_user: The border is status/error, also on hover; the sentence is in nph-field.

error-focus.changes_for_user: The border stays status/error and the halo is focus/halo-error.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity on color/muted, with the color/input border; it does not respond and wins over the error.

business_rules: The end icon always clears the value; swapping the icon changes only the art.
The clear button shows only when there is a value; after clearing, the focus goes back to the field.
Typing and clearing fire the native input and change; setting value from code fires nothing.
Enter submits the form, through its default button, as a native field does.
disabled wins over invalid: no error look on a field the person cannot edit.
domain_errors: invalid: the value needs correction; nph-field writes the sentence and passes it as description.

tokens.border: border/width, in color/input, color/input-hover, focus/border or status/error
tokens.padding: space/control-padding; the end one is input/clear-padding-end in compact
tokens.focus: focus/border, focus/halo, focus/halo-error, focus/ring-width, focus/radius-control, focus/border-radius-control and focus/radius-control-with-border

ai_hints: Use nph-input for a one-line value; for multi-line text, a password, a number or a mask, nph-input is not the piece.
Put nph-input inside nph-field when the field needs a label, help or an error message; on its own, give it a name with nph-label for or label.
Never use the placeholder as the only name.
To show an error, set the error of nph-field; do not set invalid on the input alone.
Read the value from the host on input or change; do not listen for an nph-* event.
Use icon-end with clear-label only when the person will often clear the value.
Use the same size for every field and the button of one form.
Use compact only for the search of the compact nph-toolbar and the compact table, never on a touch screen; never wrap it in a box that clips overflow, or the focus ring of its clear button is cut.

accessibility.semantics: The native input inside the shadow root, of the chosen type. The host is form-associated and labelable.
accessibility.accessible_name: From the label associated with the host: nph-label for, or a label element, referenced by the inner field. Without one, from label. The placeholder is not a name. With no name at all, the field renders and warns in development.
keyboard: Tab enters the field and, when there is a value, the clear button.
Enter in the field submits the form.
Enter or Space on the clear button clears the value and brings the focus back to the field.
accessibility.focus: The field shows the focus border and the halo whenever it has the focus, by pointer or keyboard; the clear button shows its own only for the keyboard.
accessibility.contrast: The color/input border meets 3:1 against the background (WCAG 1.4.11); the halo is decoration.
accessibility.color_alternative: The error is said by the sentence of nph-field, read as the description of the field; the border color is not the only signal.

invalid_combinations: A type outside text, email, tel, url and search — the field draws nothing.
A size outside compact, default and large — the field draws nothing.
An icon value outside none and the core names — the field draws nothing.
icon-end without clear-label — the field renders without the clear button.
invalid without the sentence in nph-field — red with no text.
anti_patterns: Painting the regular field with color/muted: it is the disabled background.
Using the halo alone with the gray border: the border is what meets 3:1.
Putting the error message inside the field.
Using the placeholder as the only label.
Using compact on a touch screen.
Clipping the overflow of a compact field: the focus ring of the clear button goes past it.
